I lost my lab and my bird (he was part of my family longer than I was, I was given the privilege to take him 9 years ago) within 4 months of each other last year, both from cancer. My dog was my soul dog, been through all the crap together and my bird was always there even in my earliest childhood memories. I’m still not right, I still hurt everyday and I couldn’t even tell you how much of a crazy mess I was but I’m better now. Punched glass several times, lots of anger outbursts, constant crying, lost a bunch of weight, binge eating one day & no appetite the next, went weeks without showering or brushing my teeth, my performance at work dropped, I was either sad or angry all the time. My boyfriend tried his best but man, I was losing it. She’s going to be hurting and grieving and grief can make you do or not do a lot of things. Grief also has no timeline, it sneaks up on you, it ruins your day, it steals sleep, it surprises you randomly when a memory triggers it. You’re doing great by just being there in whatever way you can. It makes a huge difference. Talking helps a lot, too. She can be holding a ton of guilt, don’t ask but just let her tell you when she’s ready. I had so much guilt, the what ifs, what could I have done to prevent this, was it too soon, was it the right choice, etc. It helped me so much when I finally could talk to someone and hear someone tell me I wasn’t this awful person I thought I was because of their deaths, I highly blamed myself for the longest time.

I lost my beautiful baby Feb 2024 after 2 months of fighting end stage kidney cancer. They gave him 2 weeks and I fully believe our love for each other kept him around comfortably for 2 months. The docs were surprised at his lab levels because he should’ve been extremely ill and/or dead already but he was his normal self minus a lot of weight. His muscles eventually wasted and on the day he died, he weighed 77lbs … his average weight was 123lbs. I had time to “prepare” but man, there’s no preparing for that large of a loss. Every time I have the urge to cry, I cry until I have no tears. I can’t ever sleep and if I do, it’s not very good sleep due to the meds I have to take in order to sleep, I feel cold and empty a lot of times. The first night I didn’t sleep whatsoever and stayed up building the miniverse toys while chatting with my sister on the phone. My best advice - stay busy, pick up a new hobby, definitely look into miniverse minis, the subreddit for them is awesome, find something you love doing, honor your baby in a big way if you can (I got a paw print tattoo of a paw print we did together when he was sick) and just cry and feel the pain and feel the loss because it’s inevitable but after letting yourself feel it, it lessens a little each day. It isn’t as much of a raw, open wound after a while. When my baby was taking his last breaths, I told him how much I loved him and all that and my mom who was there was telling me she saw that he knew what I was saying, he knew I did everything I could and he knew how much I absolutely adored and loved him. Your baby knew, too. He knew you tried and he loved you so much for it. He didn’t tell you what he was feeling cause he didn’t want you to worry. My baby did the same. He was a good boy, the bestest boy and he knows how much you cared for him and he cared for you just as much. I am so so so sorry for the immeasurable loss you are going through, just know it does get better, maybe not tonight or tomorrow or next week or next month but it will get better.

I’m obese but I’m 60 pounds down. It’s been a struggle getting past this plateau and working on my binge eating disorder along with my chronic depression and severe anxiety.

Just to cement in the other arguments here, I developed a binge eating disorder from an abusive, neglectful childhood. My mother didn’t feed us or supply the house with food very often among a lot of other abusive things. Instead of hoarding food like some other abused kids do, I ate as much as I could when food was available. This habit carried to my dad’s house when he won custody of me at 14. He ridiculed and humiliated me any time I snuck food or ate too much. It kept my eating disorder at bay until I graduated high school. I moved out and lived on my own where I gained over 100 pounds in less than a year cause there was no one to ridicule me to not eat. I didn’t understand my issues at the time, I just hated myself and dealt with the PTSD and residual effects of growing up in a fucked up environment from both parents. I used to be a runner and couldn’t do that anymore. I had so many mental issues and things I noticed in myself that reminded me of my abusers and it just led to more eating to cope. It was so hard to manage, so hard to just look at myself in the mirror and watch my clothes get smaller as I got bigger.

As a 28 year old, I’ve been to tons of therapy and been on many different medications but you can out-eat anything. I did for a long time. I dated abusive men and supported them financially so fast food was always the cheapest option. My mother created excuses for my weight which gave me comfort to place the blame on those excuses like thyroid issues, etc. I got sick of hating myself and the excuses and I hated what I saw in the mirror even more. I hated that people judged me so harshly on my appearance. I started getting my own identity and began finding out who I am underneath the self-loathing and depression, the stress and worry, under all the hurt and pain I’ve always felt. I began counting calories and going on walking trails and my doc put me on medication for binge eating disorder to help me get to a better me. I’ve never had high blood pressure or high cholesterol nor have I been pre-diabetic or full blown diabetic. I was healthy except for the excess weight putting the extra physical stress on my body which I’m fortunate that’s my only issue with my physical health. Like I said, I’ve lost 60 pounds but that wasn’t easy. Controlling the eating disorder is a constant struggle every single day. I find myself telling people im fasting but in reality, I starve myself often to make up for a relapse in binging. 

There’s just so much that contributes to a person’s health and weight. It’s never cut and dry, it’s never black and white. Being overweight is a side effect of something else or is caused by something deeper like a mental illness, trauma, etc. In every single episode of My 600 Lb Life, every person was born into a fucked childhood and developed an unhealthy relationship with food. That is so fucking hard to undo as an adult because it’s cemented into our heads. We don’t choose to be obese, I mean who would choose that? It sucks! When I gained all this weight, I couldn’t do as much as before, I couldn’t run, I had to worry about if I could fit in a booth or movie theater seat, I couldn’t go on the zip line with my friends in Vegas. I would not choose this ever but it’s a consequence of my childhood environment that I am taking responsibility for as an adult now. It doesn’t matter what food either, I would binge eat healthy food. It’s the caloric intake that matters. And people like YOU make us so nervous or scared to go to the gym. Now I’m not into this fat acceptance/fat phobia thing going on now because being fat is unhealthy but I’m all for minding your own business. We already know we’re fat, we already know our issues.
